hints: Focus on what the yellow precipitate tells you, this is the iodoform test for a very specific alcohol group.
The positive group for an alcohol is $\text{CH}_3\text{CH(OH)}-$, so draw the $\text{C}_5$ skeletons that contain this unit.
Two different carbon skeletons work here, and each one has a chiral centre, so remember to double each for the pair of enantiomers.
walkthrough:
**Recall the iodoform condition**

Great start, the yellow precipitate with alkaline $\text{I}_2(aq)$ is $\text{CHI}_3$, iodoform. For alcohols, only molecules containing the group $\text{CH}_3\text{CH(OH)}-$ give a positive result.

Test group:
$$\text{CH}_3-\text{CH(OH)}-\text{R}$$

**Find the C5H12O alcohols with that group**

Now fit that group into a total of 5 carbons. There are only two structural possibilities.

1. $\text{CH}_3\text{CH(OH)CH}_2\text{CH}_2\text{CH}_3$, pentan-2-ol
2. $\text{CH}_3\text{CH(OH)CH(CH}_3\text{)CH}_3$, 3-methylbutan-2-ol

**Check for chirality and count stereoisomers**

Both molecules have a chiral carbon at C2, bonded to four different groups ($\text{H}$, $\text{OH}$, $\text{CH}_3$ and a different alkyl chain). So each exists as a pair of enantiomers.

Total count:
$$2 \text{ (from pentan-2-ol)} + 2 \text{ (from 3-methylbutan-2-ol)} = 4$$

**Rule out the close traps**

Pentan-3-ol, $\text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{CH(OH)CH}_2\text{CH}_3$, looks similar but the $\text{OH}$ carbon is joined to two $\text{CH}_2$ groups, not a $\text{CH}_3$, so it is negative. Tertiary alcohols like 2-methylbutan-2-ol cannot be oxidised to the methyl ketone, so they are also negative.

options.A: 2 counts only the two structural isomers and forgets stereoisomerism. Both pentan-2-ol and 3-methylbutan-2-ol are chiral, so each counts twice.
options.B: 3 is a common miscount where you double one isomer for enantiomers but forget the other is also chiral. In fact both qualifying structures have a stereocentre at C2.
options.C: 4 is correct: 2 enantiomers of pentan-2-ol plus 2 enantiomers of 3-methylbutan-2-ol. All contain the essential $\text{CH}_3\text{CH(OH)}-$ group for the iodoform reaction.
options.D: 5 overcounts by wrongly including an extra alcohol such as pentan-3-ol or 2-methylbutan-2-ol. Pentan-3-ol lacks $\text{CH}_3\text{CH(OH)}-$, and the tertiary alcohol cannot give iodoform.
